q: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and changes its _____.
e: A simple machine amplifies force magnitude and changes its position to make work easier.

q: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and _____.
e: The six classical simple machines include the wedge, along with lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, and screw.

q: The ratio of load to effort is defined as the _____ of the machine.
e: Mechanical advantage (MA) is formally defined as the ratio of load (L) to effort (E).

q: The formula for mechanical advantage is _____.
e: Mechanical advantage is calculated by dividing the load (L) by the effort (E).

q: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the _____ of the machine.
e: Velocity ratio (VR) is the ratio of the distance moved by the effort to the distance moved by the load in the same time.

q: The formula for velocity ratio is _____.
e: Velocity ratio is calculated as the distance moved by effort ($S_{effort}$) divided by the distance moved by load ($S_{load}$).

q: The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the _____ of the machine.
e: Efficiency is precisely defined as the ratio of output work to input work.

q: Efficiency is generally expressed in the _____ form.
e: In physics and engineering, efficiency is typically multiplied by 100% and expressed as a percentage.

q: The relationship between efficiency, mechanical advantage, and velocity ratio is efficiency = _____.
e: Efficiency can be derived as the ratio of mechanical advantage to velocity ratio, multiplied by 100%.

q: In practice, the efficiency of a machine must always be _____ 100%.
e: It is impossible to build a perfect machine; input work always exceeds output work, making efficiency less than 100%.

q: Input work always exceeds output work because some effort is spent in overcoming _____.
e: In practice, some effort is always spent in overcoming friction present in the machine.

q: Work obtained from a machine when lifting a load is called the _____ work.
e: The work done on the load by the machine is defined as the output work.
